requirements.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured across node1 (writable primary), node2, and node3 (standbys)
requirements.summary: node1 was initialized and configured as primary (wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, replicator role created). node2 and node3 were provisioned via pg_basebackup -R against node1 and started as standbys. pg_stat_replication on the primary shows both walreceiver connections in 'streaming' state; pg_stat_wal_receiver on each standby confirms status=streaming from 10.100.122.10. A test table (repl_check) inserted on the primary was observed present on both standbys, and node1 confirmed pg_is_in_recovery=f (writable) while node2/node3 report pg_is_in_recovery=t.

requirements.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a certificate authority created for this cluster
requirements.summary: A self-signed CA (CN=pg-cluster-ca) was generated on node1 under /etc/pgsql-ca, and per-node server certs plus a client cert for the replicator role were issued from it and distributed to node2/node3. postgresql.conf on all nodes sets ssl=on with the node's CA-issued cert/key and shared ssl_ca_file. Live pg_stat_ssl output joined with pg_stat_replication shows ssl=t for both standby connections with cipher TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, and the standby primary_conninfo specifies sslmode='verify-full' with the CA-issued client cert/key.

requirements.requirement: Replication connections accepted only from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
requirements.summary: pg_hba.conf on node1 was edited to remove the default password-based (scram-sha-256) and peer-based replication entries and replaced with 'hostssl replication replicator <peer-ip>/32 cert clientcert=verify-full' for each of the three cluster IPs, plus a catch-all 'hostnossl ... reject' fallback. Live streaming replication connections show client_dn=/CN=replicator (issued by the cluster CA). An explicit attempt from node2 to connect to the replication database without presenting a client certificate was rejected ('no pg_hba.conf entry'), consistent with the clientcert=verify-full requirement blocking uncertificated peers.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state, for all three nodes
requirements.summary: For each of node1 (primary), node2, and node3: a pre-restart boot_id and healthy state (postgresql-16 active, correct recovery role) was captured, a native reboot was issued and acknowledged, the node briefly became unreachable, and a distinct post-restart boot_id was observed (node1: 4999270d...->46f03784...; node2: 55595e92...->531c803c...; node3: 31949c21...->cd9f2a63...), matching the fixed lifecycle snapshot's before/after-executor boot-identity cross-check. Post-restart, all nodes show postgresql-16 active, correct recovery status, TLS+cert replication reconnected (node1 shows both walreceivers streaming with client_dn=/CN=replicator), and repl_check data (including a new post-restart row inserted on the primary) present on both standbys.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly demonstrated with evidence: TLS-secured streaming replication from node1 to node2/node3 using a cluster-created CA, with pg_hba.conf restricting replication access to hostssl connections presenting a CA-issued client certificate (verify-full), and rejection of an uncertificated connection attempt. The independently required node-restart protocol was completed on all three nodes with matching boot-identity changes and confirmed post-restart recovery of replication and data, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. A handful of failed intermediate commands during pg_basebackup setup were troubleshooting/corrective in nature and did not leave harmful residue.
limitations: The cert-only enforcement test relied on an indirect signal ('no pg_hba.conf entry' when no client cert was supplied) rather than an explicit test showing a valid connection accepted only when a CA-issued cert is present versus rejected with a non-CA-issued cert; no test with a non-cluster-CA-issued certificate was captured.

Only node2 and node3 connecting to node1 were exercised in live replication traffic; the node1-self hostssl rule was configured but not separately exercised since node1 is primary-only in this topology.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed executor commands chronologically for state changes. Most mutations map directly to the task: repo/package installs, initdb, CA/cert generation and distribution with correct ownership/permissions, postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf edits, firewalld port openings, role creation, pg_basebackup provisioning, and the mandated node-restart sequence. Several failed intermediate attempts occurred while getting pg_basebackup to succeed on node2: an unrecognized --sslmode flag (cmd-d21f735ab55e4d0b, which also did 'rm -rf' on an already-empty, not-yet-initialized standby data directory - low risk, no residue), a 'No route to host' failure diagnosed and fixed by adding /etc/hosts entries and opening firewalld port 5432 (cmd-b1b56b789ed64ed8, cmd-2287919ed7404898, cmd-e0140fff895a4ce4), and a permission-denied failure on pg_hba.conf.orig that was corrected by fixing ownership on node1 (cmd-f5bf73ff96204478, cmd-3c518d883adf480e). These were bounded, low-risk troubleshooting steps directly in service of completing the base backup, not unrelated experiments, and left no harmful residue (the leftover pg_hba.conf.orig backup file replicated into standby data directories is a minor, low-risk artifact rather than unwanted state). No failed/conflicting services, no broad or destructive mutations, and no weakened security controls were observed in the final state (after_executor snapshot shows no failed-services on any node).
